extracted.intended_audience: researchers, reviewers and students conducting critical appraisal of qualitative healthcare research (e.g., systematic reviewers, clinicians, policy makers, students)
extracted.subtask_description: Use CASP's checklist to appraise the validity, results, and usefulness of qualitative research studies, answering Yes/No/Can't Tell for each question and recording an appraisal summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear statement of aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Was there a clear statement of the aims of the research?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider what the goal of the research was and why it was thought important; assess the stated relevance of the aims. (Answer choices: Yes / No / Can't Tell.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of qualitative methodology
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the research seeks to interpret or illuminate participants' actions and/or subjective experiences and whether qualitative methods are the right way to address the research goal. (Yes / No / Can't Tell.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of research design
rubrics_metrics.description: Was the research design appropriate to address the aims of the research?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the researcher justified the research design (e.g., discussed how they decided which method to use) and whether the chosen design aligns with the aims. (Yes / No / Can't Tell.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment strategy appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Was the recruitment strategy appropriate to the aims of the research?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the researcher explained how participants were selected, why the selected participants were appropriate to access the sought knowledge, and whether recruitment issues (e.g., why some people did not take part) are discussed. (Yes / No / Can't Tell.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection addressed the research issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Was the data collected in a way that addressed the research issue?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the setting for data collection was justified; how data were collected (e.g., focus group, semi-structured interview); whether methods were justified and made explicit (e.g., topic guides, interview conduct); whether methods were modified during the study and if changes were explained; the form of data (recordings, video, notes); and whether data saturation was discussed. (Yes / No / Can't Tell.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher–participant relationship considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the relationship between researcher and participants been adequately considered?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the researcher critically examined their own role, potential bias and influence during formulation of research questions and data collection (including recruitment and choice of location), and how the researcher responded to events during the study and the implications of any changes to the research design. (Yes / No / Can't Tell.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical issues considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Have ethical issues been taken into consideration?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether there are sufficient details about how the research was explained to participants to assess ethical standards; whether issues such as informed consent, confidentiality, and effects on participants during and after the study are discussed; and whether ethics committee approval was sought. (Yes / No / Can't Tell.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigour of data analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Was the data analysis sufficiently rigorous?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether there is an in-depth description of the analysis process; if thematic analysis is used, whether it is clear how categories/themes were derived from the data; whether the researcher explains how presented data were selected from the original sample to demonstrate analysis; whether sufficient data are presented to support findings; to what extent contradictory data are taken into account; and whether the researcher critically examined their own role, potential bias and influence during analysis and selection of data. (Yes / No / Can't Tell.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a clear statement of findings?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the findings are explicit; whether there is adequate discussion of evidence both for and against the researcher's arguments; whether credibility of findings is discussed (e.g., triangulation, respondent validation, multiple analysts); and whether findings are discussed in relation to the original research question. (Yes / No / Can't Tell.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Value and usefulness of the research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the researcher discusses the study's contribution to existing knowledge or understanding (for practice, policy, or relevant literature), whether new areas for research are identified, and whether the researchers discuss transferability of findings to other populations or other potential uses of the research. (Yes / No / Can't Tell.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency: use of 'Can't Tell' and avoiding assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction to never make assumptions about what researchers have done; use the 'Can't Tell' response when methods or actions are not explicit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If information is not possible to tell, select 'Can't Tell'. Many 'Can't Tell' responses may indicate lack of transparency and reduce trustworthiness of findings — interpret study results with caution. This guidance applies throughout the checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appraisal summary (positives, negatives, unknowns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarise key points from the critical appraisal that affect assessment of validity and usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise list of positive/methodologically sound aspects, negative/relatively poor methodology aspects, and unknowns to inform decision-making about the study's validity and applicability.
